title: Slow breathing impacts inter-organ dynamics modulating brain function and risk behavior
title_zh: 慢呼吸影响器官间动力学，调节大脑功能与风险行为
abstract: Successful decision-making requires that external information be interpreted in the context of the body's state. Within the framework of body-brain interaction, deliberately modifying one's autonomic state can shape how we evaluate the world, ultimately influencing choices. Yet, it remains unclear whether and how intentional autonomic regulation affects human decision-making. In this study, we tested instructed use of prolonged exhalation, a slow-breathing technique designed to boost parasympathetic activity during risky decision-making. Participants followed distinct breathing protocols while making risky choices, with neural and physiological activity measured using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and multichannel monitoring. Prolonged exhalation increased risky choices by enhancing reward sensitivity and elevating cardiac parasympathetic activity. Importantly, individuals with greater parasympathetic upregulation also showed stronger reward-related responses in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex and precuneus. Our work reveals the transformative role of breathing-based interventions, demonstrating that autonomic regulation via breathing can shape value-based decision-making through neuro-cardiac pathways.
abstract_zh: 成功的决策需要将外部信息解释为身体状态的上下文。在身体-大脑相互作用框架下，刻意改变自主神经状态可以塑造我们评估世界的方式，最终影响选择。然而，尚不清楚有意的自主调节是否以及如何影响人类决策。本研究测试了使用延长呼气的指令性慢呼吸技术，该技术旨在在风险决策期间提升副交感神经活动。参与者在做出风险选择时遵循不同的呼吸方案，并通过功能磁共振成像（fMRI）和多通道监测记录神经和生理活动。延长呼气通过增强奖励敏感性和提升心脏副交感神经活动，增加了风险选择。值得注意的是，副交感神经上调更明显的个体在腹内侧前额叶皮层和顶后叶的奖励相关反应也更强。我们的工作揭示了基于呼吸的干预的变革性作用，证明通过呼吸进行自主调节可以通过神经-心脏通路塑造基于价值的决策。
